fixed-projection.title: Fixed projection · PF-2
fixed-projection.summary: One barrel + three removable bonded cells
fixed-projection.intro: Center and bond each of the first three lenses in its own short cell on the bench, then install the cells in one common barrel. The large v0.3 glass flanges are removed.
stages: Bench preassembly
Seat, optically center, locally bond and cure L1, L2 and L3 in their own cells; recheck before assembly. L3 has front-open adhesive windows.
Barrel assembly
Complete the deeper optical stack first, then install L3, L2 and L1 cells. Each cell seats against its own metal shoulder.
fixed-projection.fixing: Glass is locally bonded to its cell. Each cell locates by its outer cylinder and rear face, and locks into the barrel with an external thread. No master ring is required for L1; thread teeth are omitted.
fixed-projection.load_path: Each lens to its own cell shoulder; each cell to its own barrel metal shoulder. Neighboring glass elements do not transmit the locking preload.
fixed-projection.note: Nine mechanical parts and a 1 mm stop land. L1/L2 use the earlier demo outlines; L3 keeps only its small prior rim. Service replaces a lens-cell assembly; glass-only replacement requires debonding.
fixed-projection.status: User-run and reviewed in SolidWorks 2023 / FreeCAD

film-projection.title: Film projection · Film
film-projection.intro: L2 is the largest lens. The stack loads through one opening; the smaller L1 is first secured in an independent adapter.
stages: Preassemble L1
Seat L1 in its adapter and secure it against the rear shoulder with the small retaining ring.
Load through the main opening
L5 → spacer → L4 → spacer → L3 → spacer → L2 → L1 adapter assembly → main retaining ring.
film-projection.fixing: Bores center the elements. Shoulders and spacers establish axial positions at the chosen contact radii. L1 has a local clamping path inside its adapter.
film-projection.load_path: Main ring → L1 adapter → L2 → spacer → L3 → spacer → L4 → spacer → L5 → barrel rear shoulder.
film-projection.note: Some contact bands intersect exported baseline ray segments. This known limitation remains in the demo. Its download contains mechanics; use the source STEP for the glass.
film-projection.status: User-run and reviewed in SolidWorks 2023 / FreeCAD

micro-objective.title: Microscope objective · 63X
micro-objective.summary: Five short preassembled cells inside one barrel
micro-objective.intro: Avoid aligning and bonding several close groups inside a deep bore. Assemble and cure each group in a short cell on the bench, then load all five cells into the common barrel.
stages: Bench assembly
Insert each optical group from the −Z opening of its cell, seat and center it in a fixture, then apply and cure local adhesive bonds.
Load complete cells
From the +Z specimen-side opening, insert the G1, G2, G3, G4 and G5 cells in order, followed by the main retaining ring.
micro-objective.fixing: Common Ø18 cell exteriors establish barrel centering. Individual shoulders and bonds hold the glass. The main ring compresses metal cell end faces rather than the glass stack.
micro-objective.load_path: Nose retaining ring → G5 cell → G4 cell → G3 cell → G2 cell → G1 cell → barrel end shoulder.
micro-objective.note: −Z faces the tube lens; +Z faces the specimen. STOP lies on a curved G3 surface, so no separate flat metal stop is added. Original glass outlines are retained.
micro-objective.status: User-run and reviewed in SolidWorks 2023 / FreeCAD

phone.title: Phone lens · 6P
phone.intro: Choose three main bore diameters first, then extend only the required peripheral lens rims. Avoid giving every lens a large common flange or using miniature threaded retainers.
stages: Load from the image side
L1 → spacer → L2 → spacer → L3 → spacer → L4 → L5 → L6.
Secure the tail ring
Keep all contacts seated in a fixture, then locally bond the tail ring to the housing and cure it.
phone.fixing: Three simple rectangular spacers set the first gaps. Peripheral contact rims link the later lenses. Tail-ring adhesive connects the ring to the barrel rather than bonding every lens.
phone.load_path: Tail ring → lens and spacer stack → front seat → barrel.
phone.note: L1/L3/L4/L5 use revised mechanical rims with the original optical bodies retained. The filter is a reserved space only. Mold release, adhesive and stress details need further design.
phone.status: User-run and reviewed in SolidWorks 2023 / FreeCAD

slr.title: SLR lens · three barrels v5
slr.summary: Thick pilot joints + one-sided spacer stacks
slr.intro: Three structural barrels enclose the optical components. Front and rear stacks use substantial spacers. Two preassembled cells remain in the middle barrel, with one thin G8 cell in the rear.
stages: Front barrel: object-side loading
G2 → tapered spacer → G1 → front retaining ring.
Middle barrel: load complete cells
Bench-assemble the G3/G4 and G5/G6 cells. From the same front opening, insert G5/G6 first, G3/G4 second, then the common retaining ring.
Rear barrel: image-side loading
G7 → long spacer → G8 cell → short spacer → G9 → cup spacer → G10 → rear retaining ring.
slr.fixing: G3/G4, G5/G6 and G8 are locally bonded within their cells. Other groups use shoulders, spacers and rings. The stop is integral with the teal middle barrel and has a finite aperture land.
slr.load_path: Rear ring → G10 → spacer → G9 → spacer → G8 metal cell → spacer → G7 → rear-barrel shoulder. G8 glass does not carry the full stack preload.
slr.note: Version 5 removes thin bridges at the joints. Minimum uncut meridional wall distances: front 8.98, middle 8.10, rear about 8.47 mm. These are geometric checks, not stress qualification.
slr.status: User-run and reviewed in SolidWorks 2023 / FreeCAD

wide-angle.title: Wide-angle lens · two barrels
wide-angle.intro: G1–G3 load from the object side of the front barrel. G4–G7 load from opposite ends of the rear barrel around its integral stop. No additional optical cells or local lens bonding are needed in this demo.
stages: Front barrel: object-side loading
G3 → spacer → G2 → G1 → front ring. G1 and G2 directly contact at the new peripheral bearing band.
Rear barrel: load from both ends
Object side: G5 → spacer → G4 → middle ring. Image side: G6 → spacer → G7 → rear ring.
Join the barrels last
Finish both subassemblies and secure their rings before mating the 10 mm pilot joint. The rear barrel's front ring must be accessed before joining.
wide-angle.fixing: Rectangular spacers are approximately 2.37 / 3.27 / 2.34 mm long. The integral stop has a 1 mm aperture land and an image-side 45° relief bevel.
wide-angle.load_path: Front ring → G1 → G2 → spacer → G3 → front-barrel shoulder. The two rear-barrel rings independently clamp their stacks against integral seats.
wide-angle.note: G2/G3/G4/G7 have extended mechanical rims; the original clear-aperture sag is preserved. Both uncut barrel bodies have at least 4 mm minimum meridional wall distance.
wide-angle.status: User-run and reviewed in SolidWorks 2023 / FreeCAD

double-gauss-focus.title: Double Gauss 50 mm F1.8 · manual focus
double-gauss-focus.summary: Whole-unit focus · short helicoid ring · 4.5 mm travel
double-gauss-focus.intro: Seven elements in five groups sit in the blue optical barrel. The teal fixed housing also provides guidance. The gold focus ring rotates and translates through a helicoid, driving the barrel through a thrust coupling while the optics retain their spacing and orientation.
stages: Preassemble the optics
Front: G2, thick spacer, G1 and front retainer. Rear: G3, thick spacer, G4, thick spacer and G5; one rear retainer closes the stack.
Insert into the fixed housing
Attach the mount envelope, insert the optical barrel from the front and engage two guide screws in its closed axial slots.
Build the thrust coupling
Fit the rear washer, wind in the focus ring, then fit the front washer, keeper and lock screw. The ring rotates; the optical barrel only translates.
Check the complete travel
0–270° gives 0 to −4.5 mm travel. Check guidance, engagement and stops; real distance markings require optical calibration.
double-gauss-focus.fixing: Shoulders, thick spacers and front/rear retainers locate the optics. Two washers and a keeper capture the focus-ring lip and transmit axial motion in both directions.
double-gauss-focus.load_path: Manual rotation → housing/ring helicoid → thrust coupling → optical barrel. Guide screws in straight axial slots prevent barrel rotation.
double-gauss-focus.note: Custom single-start left-hand trapezoidal helicoid, 6 mm lead. The Canon EF rear interface is a purchased-part envelope. Zero degrees is not calibrated infinity; mirror clearance, backlash, tolerances and preload remain to be checked.
double-gauss-focus.status: CAD macros run and reviewed; native motion and assembly paths sampled
